canonical_name: National High School Journal of Science
organizer: National High School Journal of Science (independent, student-run initiative)
eligibility_verbatim: The journal publishes original research by high school students across all scientific disciplines. Primary author must be a high school student (grades 9-12).
turkey_access_reasoning: No geographic or nationality restriction appears anywhere on the site; submission is via an online manuscript portal; the journal explicitly frames itself as accepting research from high schoolers broadly, not just US students.
international_access_notes: Fully online submission. English-language manuscript implied by academic-journal norms (not explicitly restated on the pages fetched). No country restriction found.
peer_review_notes: Own site states: 'Our peer-review process provides valuable feedback and mentorship from experts in the field.' Site also references an 'Editorial Review Process' page and (per third-party summaries) a Scientist Advisory Board of professional researchers plus student peer reviewers; full text of that subpage was not captured directly.
cost_notes: Widely and consistently corroborated as free to submit and free to publish, with no fee of any kind. The specific 'no fee' sentence was not literally present on the homepage text captured, but no fee was mentioned anywhere across all sources and this is the journal's well-known reputation.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Our peer-review process provides valuable feedback and mentorship from experts in the field.

notes_uncertainties: Already well-known in this space; confirmed not on the excluded duplicate list. Recommend a follow-up fetch of the dedicated Submission Guidelines subpage to lock down exact formatting rules and re-confirm the fee-free statement verbatim before marking PRODUCTION_READY.

organizer: Curieux Review (self-described youth-led organization; started as Curieux Academic Journal, California)
eligibility_verbatim: We accept submissions from middle school, high school, and undergraduate students only.
turkey_access_reasoning: No geography restriction stated anywhere on the site; based in Los Angeles but no residency/nationality requirement mentioned; submission is online.
international_access_notes: No language requirement stated explicitly, but MLA-format English academic writing is implied by norms.
peer_review_notes: Own site's own language does NOT use the term 'peer review' or 'peer-reviewed' anywhere in the submissions text retrieved: 'Each paper is vetted for academic integrity, factual certitude, and grammatical correctness. Once a decision is made, editors will work together to advise for admission or rejection.' This describes in-house editorial vetting, not an external academic peer-review process. Treat any marketing elsewhere that calls this 'peer-reviewed' with caution.
current_cycle_label: rolling (fast-track: ~3 weeks; seasonal: next issue release)
cost_notes: $200 publication fee (seasonal review track) charged ONLY upon acceptance, or $250 for a fast-track review (~3-week turnaround). 'If any author is in need of financial aid, please email us and we will work to accommodate your needs.' Reported acceptance rate 60-70% per third-party sources (not confirmed first-party).

evidence.raw_excerpt: We accept submissions from middle school, high school, and undergraduate students only... $200 publication fee... If any author is in need of financial aid, please email us and we will work to accommodate your needs.
no new papers will be published here going forward — this old domain is now a read-only archive; current submissions go to curieuxreview.com.

notes_uncertainties: FLAG FOR REVIEWER: this is a fee-charging (pay-upon-acceptance) student journal, not a traditional free academic journal. $200-250 is a meaningful sum for a family to weigh, and the 'review' described is in-house editorial vetting rather than described peer review by outside academic reviewers, despite the journal presenting itself with academic-journal framing. Financial aid is explicitly offered on request, and a 60-70% acceptance rate (third-party, unconfirmed) suggests it is not a rigorously selective venue. Not calling this predatory outright (real editorial process is described, financial aid exists, and it is a known/recommended option among college-counseling sites) but recommend a second reviewer explicitly weigh the fee-for-publication model before granting PRODUCTION_READY status. Distinct organization from the excluded-list journals.

eligibility_verbatim: High school students who have completed a research project within the past 1-2 years are eligible to submit. Original research only, no review articles will be accepted... co-authors (including the principal investigator/mentor of the lab) must be aware of the submission and willing to sign the Young-Scientist-Contributor-Agreement.
turkey_access_reasoning: No geographic or nationality restriction found on the official site; submission is via an online template/portal.
international_access_notes: Requires a research mentor/PI to co-sign a contributor agreement, which may be a bigger practical hurdle for a student without an established research lab relationship than for geography per se.
peer_review_notes: Own site states experts 'will examine, review, and critique your work,' and describes a roughly six-month editorial cycle from submission window close to May publication with revisions requested to strengthen manuscripts before release.
current_cycle_label: Recurring annual window historically November 1 - December 1, with publication each May; as of 2026-08-26 the site describes this as the standard pattern but did not explicitly reconfirm exact 2026 dates.
cost_notes: No fee mentioned anywhere; free to submit.

evidence.raw_excerpt: a high school student... completed a research project within the past 1-2 years... experts in an array of fields will examine, review, and critique your work.

notes_uncertainties: Requiring a signed contributor agreement from a research mentor/PI is a real practical barrier distinct from geography — a Turkey-based student without an existing mentor relationship would need one first. 3000-word cap, 3-figure/1-table limit. Currently closed; per the site's recurring pattern the next window is expected around November 2026, but this specific date was not reconfirmed for 2026 on the page fetched, so deadline is left null per the no-guessing rule.

organizer: Whitman Journal of Psychology (independent, run by and for high school students)
eligibility_verbatim: Manuscripts must follow the AP Psychology or International Baccalaureate (IB) Psychology curriculum. All research articles completed by high school students are welcome. WWJOP accepts empirical research papers, literature reviews or theoretical essays, and applied or commentary articles.
turkey_access_reasoning: No geographic/nationality restriction stated; the explicit anchor to AP or IB Psychology curricula is actually a good fit for many Turkey-based students in AP/IB-track schools, which the target user profile is likely to include.
international_access_notes: Manuscripts should follow APA 7th-edition style; framed as 'nationally recognized' in some third-party coverage but the eligibility text itself does not restrict by country.
peer_review_notes: Review process not described on the pages fetched; not claimed as 'peer-reviewed' in the text captured, so left unconfirmed rather than assumed.
current_cycle_label: Submissions closed 'due to a surplus of submissions'; site states they will reopen in Fall 2026.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Manuscripts must follow the AP Psychology or International Baccalaureate (IB) Psychology curriculum... Submissions are closed for this year. They will reopen in the Fall of 2026.

notes_uncertainties: Manuscripts must be tied to AP or IB Psychology coursework specifically — worth surfacing to students outside those two curricula that this one may not fit. Currently closed; reopens 'Fall 2026' per their own site but no exact date given.

organizer: International Youth Neuroscience Association (IYNA), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
eligibility_verbatim: The IYNA Journal is run by high school and undergraduate college students... You may not submit to the High School category if you graduated from high school before January 2026.
eligible_grades: high school (dedicated High School category exists separate from an undergraduate track)
turkey_access_reasoning: IYNA describes itself as a global organization 'inspiring high school... students worldwide'; no nationality restriction found on the submission guidelines page.
international_access_notes: Fully online submission and review process.
peer_review_notes: Own submission-guidelines page describes an editorial process, not an academic peer-review process: 'Your article will be reviewed by a senior editor and 2 junior editors' (Editing Round 1), then 'another team of 1 senior editor and 1 junior editor' for final revisions — this is student-editor review, not named external peer review. A third-party summary explicitly states the IYNA Journal 'is not a peer-reviewed journal,' consistent with what IYNA's own guidelines describe. Recording their own process description rather than upgrading it to 'peer review.'
current_cycle_label: rolling, no fixed deadline ('Deadline: Throughout the Year')
cost_notes: Free per third-party corroboration; no fee mentioned on official submission guidelines page either.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Your article will be reviewed by a senior editor and 2 junior editors... Gross deviations from the IYNA Editing and Formatting Guidelines will result in the automatic rejection.

notes_uncertainties: IYNA also runs a separate Neuroethics Essay Contest (with the International Neuroethics Society) whose entrants can opt into IYNA Journal consideration — treated here as the same underlying journal entity, not a separate record, to avoid duplication. Do NOT describe this as 'peer-reviewed' in any student-facing copy — record explicitly says it is not, despite the structured editorial process.
